findings.summary: Reviewer mutant RR2-4 SURVIVED all four suites (test_anchors_r8, test_anchors, test_verdict, test_gen_matrix): in evcore.cmd_run the --anchor-after branch's re-raise of the anchor refusal was replaced by `return 0`. The R2 fix's failure path (entry recorded, anchor refused) has no test, so per 11.4.194(6)(d)/11.4.235(D) the fix is not proven. The real code is correct (reviewer repro: anchored 4-entry ledger, delete-and-recompute, `evrec run ... --anchor-after` exits 2 anchor_disagrees, no anchor row appended, verify 2); the remediation is one test asserting exit != 0 and an unchanged anchors file, plus re-running RR2-4.

`tools/evidence/verdict --chain-only` derives PASS with exit 0 on a delete-and-recomputed ledger that has NO anchor (reviewer repro); only the JSON field 'anchor: not compared' says so. The one flag both skips the per-entry ev/1 schema (needed for the golden-bad fixtures) and accepts an absent anchor, and a caller reading the exit status sees PASS. git grep finds no production caller of --chain-only (scripts/repo/integrate_merge.sh only checks that verify exists), so non-blocking; recommend separating the two opt-ins or a distinct exit status when no anchor was compared.

`evrec run` appends a new entry onto a ledger whose existing anchor it contradicts (reviewer repro: after delete-and-recompute the run printed 'recorded seq=4' and chained new evidence onto the rewritten history before --anchor-after refused). verify still exits 2 afterwards, so detection survives; hardening: check the newest anchor before appending.

ev-anchor/1 row validation is loose: `at` is accepted when it merely ends with 'Z' (a hand row with at='Z' verified OK); a `policy` row may carry a forged probe {rewrite_rejected:true} and is accepted; duplicate JSON keys resolve last-wins ('mechanism' then 'policy' is accepted as policy). No strength bypass found (every mechanism reading is refused); this is the inherent policy limit plus misleading-row hygiene.

run_mutations.py --check labels every mutant whose edit applies as CAUGHT and prints 'mutants=241 caught=237' without running a single suite (pre-existing at HEAD; check_only returns 'CAUGHT'). A --check transcript can be misread as a kill result (11.4.273); use a distinct label such as APPLIES.

Four core mutants stay INVALID (N-I4g, N-I7e, N-I7f, W3-7; pre-existing at HEAD, their edit text no longer exists). The behaviour they guarded is still killed by live mutants: reviewer ports RR2-7 (stream redaction without patterns) and RR2-8 (named values not redacted in streams) were CAUGHT by test_evrec_r3.sh (I7 checks), RR2-9 (explicit --ledger skips blobs) CAUGHT by test_evrec_r4.sh W3-7, and the anchor-present path is killed by R8-A24/A25 and RR2-1.
